text:
marta: quick question — UX decision needed. If a user saves a per-route view that also filters on model, should the saved object include routing hints (region / capacity tier / preferred fallback)? thinking about reproducibility vs accidental hard-pinning. cc @kevin @sophie

kevin: my preference is to keep routing hints separate from the saved query payload. routing is operational and can change; coupling them makes rollouts and fallback harder. we can attach a lightweight "routingHintId" that resolves at apply-time. :thinking:

sophie: telemetry point — if we drop hints we still need to record which effective route/model combo was used when the view was applied. otherwise we lose signal for regressions. also sample rates differ by route, so saved views should carry the sampling context so analytics numbers are interpretable.

izzy: product UX: users expect "what you save = what you see". if we resolve hints dynamically the preview should show a computed snapshot (what would apply) and an explicit note "resolved routing: eu-west-1 / dedicated-high". show cost/latency delta in the preview.

kevin: agree on preview. technical sketch for saved query shape i propose:
```json
{
  "version": "v2",
  "route_id": "route_123",
  "model_filter": "gpt-open-13b:rev-2025-02",
  "filters": [{"field":"status","op":"=","value":"success"}],
  "sampling_context": {"sample_rate": 0.05, "owner":"route"},
  "routing_hint_id": "hint_987",
  "ui_meta": {"name":"Critical route - 13B failures","pinned":true}
}
```
kevin: note routing_hint_id resolves to an immutable table entry {region, tier, fallbacks} so saved queries remain small. resolves at read/apply.

marta: what about compatibility with older saved queries that have explicit routing embedded? we have lots of existing objects. migration path?

kevin: migration: on read, if old object contains inline routing, synthesize a routingHintId and write back (background migration). expose both fields in v2 read API.

sophie: telemetry events we need: "saved_view_applied" with fields [saved_query_id, resolved_routing_hint_id, model_id, model_version, effective_sample_rate, route_id, user_id]. that will let QA tie output diffs to saved view usage. also: emit "saved_view_previewed" when users open preview so we can measure confusion.

izzy: UX asks: display explicit badge when the resolved routing differs from the last-saved routing ("live routing has changed since save"). also add a small inline cost estimate using last 7d tokens for that route+model combo.

kevin: engineering caveat: computing preview cost/latency requires a bounded call to the routing service + cached perf profiles per model. ok but we should gate to console A/B for first rollout.

marta: sounds reasonable. next steps: kevin to draft API contract + migration plan; sophie to add telemetry schema; izzy to wire up preview UI copy & badges. i'll own rollout checklist and A/B blast percent.

dev-bot: deploy queued: console-preview-service @ 2187654360 — will contain routingHintId resolver endpoint (build/4567) :rocket:

kevin: I'll post the draft API RFC in #eng-platform in ~1h and link back here. :thumbsup:

sophie: adding telemetry table draft to the analytics board. anyone object to starting with sample rate as float? (0.0-1.0)

izzy: fine by me. i'll mock the preview with placeholder numbers so we can iterate on copy.

marta: thanks all — capturing decisions in the ticket now.
